paths.description: Homepage and global shell: navigation, merchandising, consent, preferences, performance, privacy and crawler visibility.
Electronics listing archetype: filters, product grid, responsive layout, SSR and discovery.
Product-detail and purchase-entry archetype: offer clarity, metadata, pricing and add-to-cart controls.
Authentication/form archetype: labels, autocomplete, account access and third-party sign-in.
Search-results archetype requested with q=laptop; edge security blocked this path and showed the production block page.

findings.summary: The cookie banner obscures a large part of the core storefront on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed black consent panel covering the product grid and lower first viewport before any user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equally clear accept/reject choices; reserve modal treatment for user-requested settings.

findings.summary: Narrow layouts overflow horizontally.
findings.evidence: At a 360px visual viewport, layout evidence reports 41px overflow on the homepage and 120px on the category listing. The mobile search capture also shows a block page rather than results.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed/minimum desktop widths with intrinsic fluid sizing, constrain children with min-width:0/max-width:100%, and verify every template at 360px.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on the first focusable control.
findings.evidence: The focus probe focused the visual-assistant link and computed outline:none and box-shadow:none on both home and category; the category also had 1,187 rendered controls smaller than 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible treatment and enlarge compact hit areas to at least the applicable WCAG target-size baseline.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is outside the good range.
findings.evidence: The raw-CDP trace measured LCP 3.85s; Lighthouse’s redirected mobile condition measured 5.7s. Both exceed the 2.5s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP element, reduce critical dependency chains and defer non-essential storefront and marketing work.

findings.summary: The listing template performs repeated long main-thread tasks.
findings.evidence: Category mobile layout observation recorded eight long tasks, including 326ms and three 260ms tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the listing work, split long tasks, defer below-fold widgets, and schedule non-urgent work by priority.

findings.summary: The initial network is heavy and includes a broad render-blocking stylesheet set.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 237 requests and 4.41MB transferred, including 14 stylesheets and nine parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheet candidates confirmed in the document head.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer template CSS not needed above the fold, rationalise preloads/preconnects, and preserve effective caching.

findings.summary: Third-party and application scripts dominate the load.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 45 scripts and 2.05MB script transfer; GTM, Google Ads, the widget list bundle, navigation and TikTok were among the largest files.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tags and unused bundles, conditionally load marketing code after consent/need, and split storefront widgets by visibility.

findings.summary: Many interactive and image elements lack accessible text alternatives.
findings.evidence: The home probe counted 7 unnamed buttons and 318 anchors without discernible text; the images primitive found 38 images without alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control an accessible name, make icon links descriptive, and add meaningful alt text or empty alt for decoration.

findings.summary: Consent actions fail minimum text contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2.78:1 for white text on the orange Accept and Reject consent buttons, below 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Darken the orange or use dark text so normal-size button labels reach at least 4.5:1 in every state.

findings.summary: Heading/landmark structure and visible focus are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1, begins with h3 before h2, exposes no nav landmark in the DOM probe, and the focused first link has no outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1, use ordered headings and nav landmarks, and implement persistent :focus-visible styling.

findings.summary: Reflow and target sizing do not remain usable at a narrow viewport.
findings.evidence: The 360px category view overflows by 120px and the probe counted 1,187 rendered interactive elements below 24px in at least one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix reflow without horizontal scrolling and size controls to provide comfortable touch targets without disabling zoom.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP policy leave avoidable security gaps.
findings.evidence: CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval; 18 of 21 cookies were flagged insecure by the cookie primitive, including analytics cookies without Secure and SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP, remove unsafe-eval, and set Secure with an intentional SameSite policy on all cookies.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party transfer are disproportionate before a consent choice.
findings.evidence: The load contacted 19 third-party origins and known DoubleClick/GTM/Google Ads trackers; HAR attributed 4.28MB of 4.41MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Default optional analytics/advertising off until consent, consolidate vendors, batch essential telemetry and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: A representative search request falls through to a generic security block page.
findings.evidence: The /sr?q=laptop path produced “Sorry, you have been blocked” instead of results or a storefront recovery state, with no in-product retry/navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Tune edge rules for legitimate search URLs and return a branded, accessible recovery page with retry, support and safe navigation.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and misses responsive formats.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 19 oversized and 64 legacy-format images; a 68px “Yemek” icon downloads a 400px 436KB GIF, the largest individual HAR resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace animated GIF with efficient video/animated WebP where appropriate and serve responsive AVIF/WebP at display resolution.

findings.summary: Substantial marketing/background work runs during the first load.
findings.evidence: The first load makes 237 requests; GTM, Google Ads, TikTok, DoubleClick and Adform execute before the user selects a consent preference.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate optional work behind consent and user intent, batch telemetry, and defer background fetches until the page is idle or visible.

findings.summary: Third-party media/script cost lacks a tight first-load budget.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 234 third-party-origin requests and 4.28MB third-party transfer, including 2.05MB scripts and 1.77MB images.
findings.suggestedFix: Set enforceable per-template budgets for scripts, images, fonts and vendors; lazy-load lower-value media and remove low-value tags.

findings.summary: The storefront ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot remains a light #fafafa storefront, and the computed probe reports color-scheme: normal with body background rgb(250,250,250).
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, controls, imagery and browser chrome with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Reusable commerce components do not expose component-level responsive rules.
findings.evidence: A live stylesheet probe found 0 @container rules while the category template overflowed by 120px at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards, filters and navigation components containment and adapt them with @container instead of relying only on page-wide breakpoints.

findings.summary: The storefront emits failed requests and browser errors during load.
findings.evidence: HAR observed ten HTTP 403 responses in storefront modal, similar-product and social-proof requests; Lighthouse also logged a 400 console network error in its redirected run.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix request eligibility and error handling so expected denials are not issued as failed browser requests; eliminate genuine console errors.

findings.summary: Image markup omits intrinsic sizing and often sends non-responsive legacy assets.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 99 of 100 images without width/height, 35 without srcset, 64 legacy-format assets and 19 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes and modern formats from the image CDN.

findings.summary: The conventional sitemap endpoint is missing.
findings.evidence: robots.txt returned 200, but /sitemap.xml returned HTTP 404. Canonicals and hreflang were otherwise present on representative pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap index, reference it from robots.txt, and keep canonical/hreflang entries consistent across storefront locales.

findings.summary: The sign-in surface offers password/federated login but no passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains username/current-password autocomplete and Google/Facebook buttons; the page contains no PublicKeyCredential/passkey signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Add conditional WebAuthn/passkey authentication and registration while retaining accessible recovery options.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header primitive found no Permissions-Policy and a CSP weakened by unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval. Clickjacking is covered by frame-ancestors and HSTS/nosniff are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and harden CSP with nonces/hashes and Trusted Types where applicable.

findings.summary: The app-like storefront does not advertise an install manifest or verified offline fallback.
findings.evidence: The probe confirms serviceWorker support in the browser but found no link rel=manifest; the site identifies itself as mobile-web-app-capable.
findings.suggestedFix: Ship a valid web app manifest and verify a useful offline fallback for product/listing shells and saved state.

findings.summary: The commerce flows expose rich metadata but no structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: Product JSON-LD accurately describes price and availability, while the home probe found no WebMCP/model-context registration.
findings.suggestedFix: For opted-in commerce use cases, expose narrowly scoped, confirmable agent tools for search, cart and order-state actions.
